newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Aleman gives ultimatum to Nicaragua war holdouts.
newsitem.headline: Aleman gives ultimatum to Nicaragua war holdouts.

text.p: New Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman on Tuesday gave the last armed gangs remaining from the country's civil war a final chance to lay down their arms and return to society or be treated like criminals.
Aleman said a government commission headed by Defence Minister Jaime Cuadra had started contacts with the armed gangs three days ago and he expected the problem to be resolved by the end of February.

"Today we make a call for reconciliation with justice to all the existing (armed) groups so that the country is governed by the rule of law," Aleman said in a news conference accompanied by army chief Gen. Joaquin Cuadra and police chief Franco Montealegre.
"We want to make clear the government's firmness that this is the last opportunity for the armed bands to put down their arms and re-integrate into civil life," he said.
Despite the end of Nicaragua's civil war in 1990, many of its former combatants later re-armed to protest the government's failure to fulfil the terms of the peace treaty.

Gen. Cuadra said about 500 members of 33 armed bands loosely linked to the former Contra rebels or Sandinista army continue to operate in parts of the north and central provinces of Jinotega, Matagalpa and Chontales.

Despite repeated government amnesties and help to return to civilian life, the problem has not gone away. Since 1990, armed bands have killed 1,000 people, wounded 400 and kidnapped 600 civilians, Cuadra said.

Aleman called on the armed bands to assemble immediately into one of three "peace zones" in these regions, in which they will be guaranteed safety, food and medicine, in preparation for negotiations with the government.
